    A branch is a project that starts as a copy of another project, its parent, and can be refilled from it later. Typical uses are a database per pull request in CI, trying a migration, or debugging against real data (V2 §8). internal/branching holds the whole lifecycle. It reuses provisioning and restores from the control plane and backups, and adds very little of its own.

    • branching684 linesCreates, resets, detaches, and expires database branches (V2 §8): shared-tier copies of a parent project, from its latest backup or live, that keep their URL and credentials across resets and delete themselves after a TTL.

    What a branch is#

    A branch is an ordinary row in projects with its own database, owner role, app password and pooler route. Seven columns, added by migration 00015, make it a branch, and an eighth says what happens to its files:

    ColumnMeaning
    parent_project_idThe parent. Not null means "is a branch". A foreign key to projects(id) only, not to (id, org_id): the code keeps the two in one organisation (see transfers).
    branch_sourcebackup or live: where it was filled from, and the default for a reset.
    branch_schema_onlyWhether it holds the parent's schema without rows. Fixed at creation. A reset keeps it.
    expires_at, expiry_notified_atWhen the sweep deletes it (null: never), and whether the 24-hour warning was sent.
    branch_backupsWhether it takes nightly backups and a final backup on delete. Off by default.
    sensitive_data"Contains sensitive data" (V2 §8.5). Shared with ordinary projects. A branch copies its parent's.
    branch_copy_filesWhether it was made with copy_files, so its resets copy the parent's stored files again. Added by migration 00077, which fills it from the create operation where that is still kept.

    How a branch relates to its parent:

    • One level deep. Resolve refuses a parent that is itself a branch.
    • Same organisation, same region, always the shared tier, on the organisation's own shared cluster if it has one, even when the parent is dedicated. It runs the parent's Postgres major (Create reads the parent's instance). Neither a branch nor a parent with live branches can be transferred to another organisation.
    • Members are a snapshot. The transaction that inserts the branch copies the parent's project members and roles (CopyProjectMembers). Its creator becomes its admin, unless they are an organisation owner or admin, who are admins of every project anyway. Later changes to the parent's members do not reach the branch, except a removal: someone removed from the parent leaves its live branches too, since they hold its data.
    • Its own credentials. The branch gets a new opaque database name, owner role and app password, shown once in the create response. A reset keeps all of them, and members' personal logins, so a DATABASE_URL in CI or a .env keeps working (TestBranchResetKeepsURL).
    • Not copied: webhooks and scheduled jobs. The xenibase schema that comes with the data is dropped or rebuilt by ResetWebhooks (see Life of a project).
    • Not promotable. Promotion refuses a branch (dedicated.Promote). Detach it first.

    Creating a branch#

    POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/branches (CreateBranch), or xenibase branch create, whose --replace deletes a branch of the same name first and whose --env prints DATABASE_URL lines for CI.

    1. Resolve. Resolve checks the request against the parent and fills the defaults. The parent must be active. A live copy needs a parent that is not asleep (a sleeping Free project refuses connections). A backup copy needs a succeeded logical backup. The TTL defaults to 7 days and must be 1 hour to 30 days, or 0 for none.
    2. Quotas. The handler checks CheckCreateBranch with the parent's latest measured size, then operations in flight (see limits).
    3. Insert and queue. Create calls provision.Create with a BranchSpec. One transaction inserts the project, sets the branch columns, copies the members, adds the creator and enqueues branch_create. The parent and options go into the operation's params as {"branch": {...}}, next to the sealed password.
    4. Backend services. If the parent has them, PrepareBranch makes the branch's API row, ref and keys now, so the response can return them once (below).
    5. Fill. The worker runs runCreate: Prepare (role, database, hardening). On a second attempt, RecreateDatabase first, to start from an empty database. Then fill, then EnableBranch, then Publish (member logins, pooler route, smoke test, active), then BranchFiles. A retry that finds the branch already active only runs what follows Publish.

    fill first runs copyExtensions. It reads the parent's extensions, and creates those in public on the branch as the admin, because the restore runs as the owner, who may not. Extensions in a schema of their own come with the dump. Then it copies from one of two sources:

    SourceHowCost to the parent
    backup (default)The newest succeeded logical, final or safety backup (LatestSucceededBackup), restored by backup.RestoreInto on the branch's agent: decrypted as it streams, pg_restore as the console login with --role the owner.None. The data is as of that backup.
    liveThe agent's /v1/copy: pg_dump of the parent as the instance admin, with --no-owner and --no-acl, piped into pg_restore as the owner on the branch (see agent commands).A full dump, now.

    Schema only passes SchemaOnly to the dump or the restore. Its default is the parent's sensitive_data, and only the parent's project admin may take a full copy of a sensitive parent:

    MayCopySensitive is the caller's effective role on the parent (the request was authorised there), so organisation owners and admins qualify. TestBranchQuotaOnPersonalPlan covers both refusals.

    Reset#

    POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/reset on the branch (ResetBranch). Reset queues branch_reset through EnqueueExclusiveTx: the branch must be active or error with nothing else in flight (one operation per project), and it moves to restoring. The caller must still have project.branch on the parent, and a full-data reset of a parent marked sensitive needs its project admin role, as for a new branch. The source is the request's, or the branch's own. A backup source needs a backup of the parent. Schema only is always the branch's own. The handler checks operations in flight first, as for a new branch.

    PgBouncer's KILL drops the branch's client and server connections, and new clients wait until RESUME instead of failing. RecreateDatabase drops the database WITH (FORCE) and makes it again with the same name and owner. The owner's SCRAM verifier lives on the role, which is not dropped, so the app password still works. SyncMemberRoles puts members' grants back. If both attempts fail, failReset resumes the route and leaves the branch in error, its data possibly partial. Another reset or a delete fixes it.

    Resolved

    A reset used to re-read the parent without asking whether the caller might still read it: the route checked project.branch on the branch only, and fill read the parent by ID. Someone removed from the parent kept a fresh dump of its current data a reset away on any branch they were copied onto, and a full branch of a parent marked sensitive afterwards kept refilling with every row for any developer on it. Now Reset checks project.branch on the parent for the caller, under the branch's lock (a token restricted to the parent still covers its branches, one restricted to the branch alone does not), and refuses a full-data reset of a sensitive parent to anyone but its project admin, the rule Resolve applies to a new branch (403 either way). And RemoveProjectMember on a parent also removes the person from its live branches (DeleteBranchMemberships) and drops their logins there, since a branch holds the parent's data (TestResetChecksTheParent, TestRemovingAParentMemberLeavesItsBranches).

    Detach, expiry and backups#

    • Detach (POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/detach, Detach) makes a new standalone project, so it gets a new project's checks: under the branch's row lock (WithIdleProject: active, nothing pending), the caller needs org.create_project and the organisation must be within its projects quota (CheckCreateProject). Then one statement, DetachBranch, clears the parent, the expiry, the warning and branch_backups. The project keeps its database, credentials, members and API. branch_source and branch_schema_only stay on the row as history.
    • Expiry moves with PATCH /api/v1/projects/{id}/settings (expires_at, or no_expiry), which needs project.settings, the admin role. SetExpiry accepts a time in the next 30 days and re-arms the warning. branch_backups goes through the same route (SetBackups).
    • The sweep, Sweep, deletes up to 100 expired branches per pass through the ordinary delete (provision.DeleteChecked), after checking under the row lock that each is still an expired branch, with no final backup unless the branch takes backups now. It then emails each creator once when less than 24 hours remain. Without SMTP the warning counts as sent. A conflict (another server got there first, or the branch was extended or detached since the list was read) is ignored, so several servers can sweep at once.
    Spec and code differ

    V2 §8.4 calls for "an hourly job". cmd/server runs the sweep every 10 minutes (branchSvc.Run), as docs/decisions.md (M13 #4) records, though the package and the comment above that line still say hourly.

    Resolved

    Detach used to make a standalone project without the checks a new project gets. It needed only project.branch, the developer role, and called neither CheckCreateProject nor org.create_project; branches don't count toward the projects quota (CountOrgProjects), so create-then-detach gave an organisation as many permanent projects as it liked, and a developer in an organisation whose members may not create projects could own one as its admin. It also took no lock and ignored the status, so a branch detached mid-reset was overwritten from its former parent once the reset continued. Now Detach runs under WithIdleProject (the branch must be active with nothing pending, 409 otherwise), checks org.create_project for the caller (403; a project-restricted token can't, as it can't create projects), and applies CheckCreateProject (409 quota_exceeded) before DetachBranch (TestDetachIsANewProject).

    Resolved

    The sweep used to delete from a list it read earlier: ExpiredBranches runs once per pass, and provision.Delete locked the row but did not look at expires_at or parent_project_id again, so a branch extended or detached between the query and its turn in the loop was deleted anyway, without a final backup unless it had taken backups when the list was read. Now each delete goes through expire, which hands DeleteChecked a check run on the locked row: it skips the branch (a conflict the sweep ignores) unless it is still a branch past its expiry, and takes skipFinalBackup from that row's branch_backups (TestSweepChecksTheLockedRow).

    Who may manage branches#

    One action covers branches: project.branch, developer and above, token scope write.

    RouteActionChecked on
    GET …/{id}/branchesproject.viewThe parent. The list then leaves out branches the caller is not a member of, or a token does not cover.
    POST …/{id}/branchesproject.branchThe parent
    POST …/{id}/resetproject.branchThe branch, then the parent in Reset (and its admin role for a full copy of sensitive data)
    POST …/{id}/detachproject.branch, then org.create_projectThe branch, then its organisation in Detach
    DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}project.delete, or project.branch on a branchThe branch
    PATCH …/{id}/settings (expiry, backups)project.settingsThe branch

    The delete row is how developers delete branches but not projects (V2 §2.3). A route rule may carry a branchAction, and the guard swaps it in when the project it resolved has a parent:

    The resolved parent also widens restricted tokens. authz.Can lets a token restricted to a project act on that project's branches, so a CI token for the parent can create, use and delete them. Lists apply the same rule through tokenAllows. A detached branch is outside the token from then on. Roles still come from project_members of the branch itself, and scopes still apply. See Security for the guard as a whole.

    Resolved

    A transfer used to break the rule that a branch and its parent share an organisation: orgs.Transfer refused neither a branch nor a parent with live branches, and fill read the parent by ID. A branch moved to organisation B stayed a branch of A's project, and B's owners and admins could reset it from live and keep receiving A's current data; a parent moved to B left its branches in A, hidden from ListBranches but still counted by CountLiveBranches, which kept B from deleting it. Now orgs.Transfer refuses a branch ("detach it to transfer it") and a parent with live branches, with a 409, after locking the row. fill fails for good when the parent is in another organisation than the branch, and Reset refuses such a branch with a 409, so a pair split before this release is never refilled; detaching it or deleting it are left. CountLiveBranches now filters by the parent's organisation, as ListBranches does (TestTransferKeepsBranchesWithTheirParent, TestBranchInAnotherOrganisationIsNotFilled).

    Branches with backend services of their own#

    When the parent has backend services (V4.1 §9.5), the branch gets an API of its own, never the parent's, so neither's tokens work on the other. cmd/server sets branching.Service.API to the services service. The work is split in two because the keys must be in the create response but the API can only be turned on once the copy is in:

    1. PrepareBranch, in the request, in one transaction: the branch's services row and a new ref, the parent's settings (exposed schemas, public tables, CORS, auth configuration and templates) without their secrets (providers_enc: SMTP, SMS, OAuth, captcha and hook secrets), and a publishable and a secret key. A failure here is logged, and the branch is still made, without an API.
    2. EnableBranch, in runCreate before the branch is published, and at the end of every reset: purgeSessions deletes the sessions, refresh tokens, flow states, one-time codes and MFA challenges that came with the data, so a parent's refresh token cannot be spent on the branch. Then the request roles, xb_* schemas and a new signing key. The parent's app users and their password hashes come with the data, so they sign in again on the branch with the same passwords.
    3. Then BranchFiles queues copy_branch_files as a background operation, when the branch was made with copy_files (remembered in branch_copy_files) or after any reset. runCopyBranchFiles reads the object versions the branch's xb_storage.objects names, which came with the data copy, and copies each one from the parent's prefix to the branch's inside the store. After a reset it first tidies the branch's prefix (below).

    TestBranchServices covers the keys, the separate signing key, the dropped sessions and the file copy.

    Resolved

    Any copy error used to count as "not found in the parent", and the operation succeeded: the loop did not tell storage.Client.Copy's ErrNotFound from a wrapped error, so throttling, a network error, an object over S3's 5 GB single-copy limit or the operation's context ending each skipped a file, the job reported success, its three attempts went unused, and the branch's rows pointed at files it did not have. Now copyObjects counts only ErrNotFound as missing. Any other error, from the Head of the destination or the copy, fails that file; the others are still tried, and the attempt then fails, saying how many were copied, already there, missing and failed, so the retry copies only what is left (it skips what Head finds). A context that ends stops the attempt at once (TestCopyBranchFilesRetriesFailures). An object over 5 GB, possible only on a plan without an upload limit, still can't be copied in one request, and now fails the operation instead of being skipped silently.

    Resolved

    A reset used to bring the parent's file rows but not their files, and strand the branch's own: runReset called EnableBranch with copyFiles false, so the refilled xb_storage.objects named parent versions the branch never had, and the objects already under the branch's prefix (copies and its own uploads) were named by no row, while the garbage list that would have removed them went with the dropped database. The storage sweep, which meters rows, did not bill them, and only the nightly reconciler would remove them, once a week old. Now a branch remembers copy_files (branch_copy_files, migration 00077), Reset carries it into the operation, and runReset notes when it drops the database and calls BranchFiles after EnableBranch. Its background copy_branch_files first runs strandedFiles: every version stored under the branch's prefix before the drop that no row or upload names goes on the new garbage list, which the next storage sweep empties through collectGarbage (it checks again that no row names it). Then, for a branch made with copy_files, it copies the parent's files again, skipping those still there (TestResetBranchFilesAreRemoved, TestResetCopiesFilesAgain).

    Limits and quotas#

    LimitWhere
    branches per organisation (Personal 10, Team 25), counting live branchesCheckCreateBranch with CountOrgBranches
    The parent's latest measured size against project_storage_mb, and the organisation's shared storage plus that size against shared_storage_mbCheckCreateBranch (fitsShared). Unmeasured parents pass.
    Organisation active, not at its spend cap, not restricted for an overdue balanceCheckCreateBranch
    Operations in flight (3 or 5), counting branch_create and branch_resetCheckOperation on create and reset (operationKinds)
    Not counted toward projectsCountOrgProjects
    A parent with live branches cannot be deletedprovision.DeleteChecked, under provision.Delete
    Neither a branch nor a parent with live branches can be transferredorgs.Transfer
    Detaching counts as creating a projectDetach: org.create_project and CheckCreateProject
    Usage: branch_hours, the fraction of each hour a branch existed (HourlyBranches), and branch_gb_hours, its measured sizetenancy usage, rated by billing (Billing)
    Resolved

    Resets used to skip the operations-in-flight limit: branch_reset is in operationKinds, so it counted against the limit, but ResetBranch never called CheckOperation, so a developer or a CI token could reset every branch at once, one full pg_dump of the parent per branch with a live source, past the 3 or 5 the plan allows. Now ResetBranch calls CheckOperation before queueing, as CreateBranch does, and answers 409 quota_exceeded beyond the limit (TestResetBranchCountsTowardsOperationsInFlight).

    Failure handling#

    What failsWhat happens
    No backup to branch from409 at request time, telling the caller to branch from live. If the backup disappears before the worker runs, the create fails permanently and rolls back.
    The parent is deleted before the fillfill fails permanently. A create rolls back. A reset leaves the branch in error (a reset asked for once the parent is deleted is refused with a 409).
    The parent is in another organisation (a pair split before transfers refused it)A reset is refused with a 409; fill fails permanently. Detach or delete the branch.
    EnableBranch fails on createThe branch is not published yet: the retry recreates and refills its database, and if that fails too, Rollback removes it as for a failed copy.
    Queueing the file copy fails after PublishThe retry finds the branch active and only queues it again. If that fails too the operation reads failed, but the branch and its API work; a reset copies the files.
    The file copy fails (other than a file missing from the parent)Retried, three attempts in all, each skipping what is copied. If it gives up, the branch's rows name files it lacks until a reset copies again.
    The copy itself (pg_dump, pg_restore, an extension the shared tier lacks)A live copy's error is permanent. A backup restore's error is retried once, on an empty database. Then Rollback soft-deletes the branch and drops its route, database and role, handing them to drop_project_objects if that fails.
    A live reset of a sleeping parentNot checked at request time, unlike create. The copy fails, and the branch ends in error.
    A reset that gives upfailReset: RESUME, status error, data possibly partial. The sweep still expires it.
    The server dies mid-resetThe attempt is retried: KILL again, recreate, refill. Clients wait at the pooler meanwhile.
    PrepareBranch failsThe branch is made and the response has no API. EnableBranch finds no services row and leaves it alone.
    The expiry email failsRetried next pass. With no SMTP it is marked sent.
    The organisation is suspendedNothing expires until it is active again.
    Resolved

    A failure after Publish used to retry against a live branch, and the rollback then did nothing. Publish marked the branch active and routed it before EnableBranch ran, so when EnableBranch failed the second attempt called RecreateDatabase, which dropped the routed database WITH (FORCE) under any connected client, without the pooler KILL it needs; if that attempt failed too, rollbackCreate saw active and returned, leaving a failed operation, an active branch and API keys that never worked. Now runCreate runs EnableBranch before Publish (the database is there and the edge serves only active projects), so its failure is retried, and rolled back, on a branch no one uses yet. Only queueing the file copy follows Publish, and a retry that finds the branch active runs only that, never Prepare or RecreateDatabase (TestCreateRetryAfterPublishKeepsTheBranch).

    Spec and code differ

    A few smaller differences, most recorded in docs/decisions.md under M13. V2 §8.2 names a branch's database <parent-db>__<branch-slug>_<rand>; branches get opaque names like every project. §8.2 step 3 applies extensions after the restore; they are created first, because the owner cannot. §8.3 pauses the route; the code uses KILL, which also drops open connections. §11 lists a branch_delete operation; a branch is deleted by the ordinary delete. §2.3's role table lets developers create, reset and delete branches; they may also detach, which the spec leaves to no particular role, when they may create projects in the organisation.

    A dedicated project has a Postgres container of its own on a node, created by that node's agent and archiving WAL with WAL-G from its first segment. Everything here builds on that container: HA adds a second member under Patroni, a read replica adds a member that never leads, a resize recreates the container with new limits, and a move builds a container elsewhere and copies the database into it by logical replication. Every long step is an operation (the operations queue); the kinds and their attempts are in Kinds.

    Dedicated instances#

    An instance is an instances row with its node, limits, volume, major, max_connections, WAL-G prefix and sealed superuser secret; the project points at it through projects.instance_id. Sizes are three profiles (Profiles) or any size a resize asks for:

    ProfilevCPUMemorymax_connections
    small (default)11 GB100
    medium24 GB200
    large48 GB400
    custom0.25 to 64512 MB to 256 GB50 per GB, 100 to 500

    The volume defaults to 20 GB (1 to 16,384). Docker local volumes cannot enforce it, so it is an allowance: what is billed and where the disk warning sits. Postgres settings follow memory, a replication slot may hold back at most a quarter of the volume in WAL (max_slot_wal_keep_size, at least 1 GB; 10 GB on an agent-run shared cluster), and the agent adds wal_level=logical and the WAL-G archive_command:

    Placement and creation#

    Validate refuses a dedicated create while no default storage target or backup key exists, then places it with placeDedicated: among the region's healthy, active dedicated or both nodes where the size fits (the agent's reported CPUs, memory and disk, less what dedicated instances there are allocated), the one with the fewest dedicated instances. The size is a profile's, or for a restore, a detached replica or a node move the source's CPUs and memory as given (CreateParams.Size), which may match no profile. When nothing fits and capacity automation is on, it asks for a new machine and the create waits up to 25 minutes for it to join (waitForHost). A node chosen by hand gets the same checks.

    Ensure is the instance half of the create flow (The control plane): it generates xenibase_admin (a point-in-time restore takes the source's, which is in the data), fixes where the archive goes, has the agent create the container, records its address, and revokes CONNECT on postgres and template1 from PUBLIC. The first base backup follows, always taken on the current leader; WAL-G keeps 7, or one per day of a longer PITR add-on (Backups, restores and imports). A restart from the Instance panel is a Recreate, a fresh container from the node's current image on the same volume. Start, stop and restart are refused with HA on.

    The orphan reaper#

    A create whose rollback could not reach the node leaves an instance behind, and so does a move's rollback that could not remove its target. Every minute ReapOrphans destroys the container, volume and WAL-G archive of each instance this returns, once its node is healthy:

    Resolved

    The reaper used to destroy the target of a running move, promotion or major upgrade. These insert the target when they are queued, and the project points at the source until the cutover commits, so five minutes after queueing the target matched every condition: the sweep destroyed it mid-copy and deleted its archive, the retry recreated an empty container under a row that kept deleted_at, and a pass that listed the target just before a cutover and removed it just after left only the stopped source. Now the query skips an instance a queued or running operation names as its target_instance, and an upgrade preflight's scratch instance in its first hour; once the operation has failed and its rollback could not remove the target, the reaper takes it. ReapOrphans runs the same query again for each instance, by id, just before destroying it, and Ensure refuses an instance already marked deleted rather than start a container under it (TestListOrphanedInstancesSkipsAnOperationsTarget, TestEnsureRefusesARemovedInstance).

    max_connections#

    MaxConnectionsFor gives 50 per whole GB, between 100 and 500, stored per instance (migration 00060). A project's connection limit may reach that less 10 kept for Xenibase's own logins (ConnectionReserve).

    PathThe new instance's max_connections
    Create, promotionFrom memory.
    Point-in-time restore, replica detachAt least the source's (MinMaxConnections): a standby will not replay WAL from a server that allowed more.
    Same-size node move, major upgradeThe larger of the formula and the source's.
    Resize, or a move that is oneFrom the new memory; FitConnectionLimit then lowers the project's limit and pool if they no longer fit.
    Under PatroniIt lives in the cluster's dynamic configuration, the same on every member, so a resize patches it in etcd first (setClusterMaxConnections).

    Resizing#

    PlanResize refuses a smaller disk and checks that the difference fits on every node holding a member. runResize writes the size onto the row and recreates. Without HA the poolers freeze the routes (Freeze: PAUSE on the transaction pooler, KILL on the session pooler) around one recreate, then replicas follow one at a time. With HA the standby and replicas go first, the project switches over, then the old primary is recreated, so writes pause only for the switchover. A disk change alone needs no restart. When the node cannot hold the new size, a project without HA or replicas is moved into an instance of the new size on another node; with them the resize is refused. failResize puts the old size back on the row and, without HA, recreates at it.

    Resolved

    A resized instance used to be impossible to restore or detach. A size that matches no profile is recorded as profile custom (profileName); a point-in-time restore and a replica detach copied that name into the new project, and Validate, looking it up in Profiles, refused with unknown profile "custom", on the path used in an incident. Now both pass the source's CPUs and memory as CreateParams.Size (SizeProfile), which Validate takes in place of a profile, names as the row will be, and checks for room on the node. A node move passes its size the same way, so a move's capacity check is now of the real size rather than of the small profile (TestDetachReplicaOfAResizedProject, TestValidateTakesAResizedSourcesSize).

    The maintenance window#

    Agents report each instance's running release and its image's, checked hourly. Every 5 minutes one server takes the sweep's advisory lock and MaintenanceSweep, inside the window (default Sunday 02:00 to 06:00 UTC), queues a minor_upgrade operation for at most one instance that is behind, and none while one is queued or running, dedicated first, skipping any with a project not active or with an operation pending (InstanceBusy). EnqueueMinorUpgrade makes it the project's exclusive operation on a dedicated instance; on a shared cluster it belongs to no project, and withIdleProject refuses its projects' exclusive operations until it ends. The operation's minorUpgrade freezes the poolers for every project on it, recreates, resumes, and records the pause. An HA instance is switched over instead (minorUpgradeHA), and only inside maintenance announced to it 72 hours ahead; the sweep drafts that announcement for the first window at least 96 hours away, for an admin to confirm.

    Resolved

    A maintenance restart used to be no operation, so nothing kept other work off the instance: the sweep checked InstanceBusy once and took no lock, so while minorUpgradeHA waited up to an hour for a recreated standby the owner could queue ha_disable or a resize on the same members, and every xenibase-server ran the loop, so two could restart instances at once or the same one twice. Now each minor upgrade is a minor_upgrade operation (runMinorUpgrade, one attempt plus one after a crash) queued through EnqueueExclusiveTx on a dedicated instance's project, or for a shared cluster under every project's row lock with withIdleProject refusing their exclusive operations meanwhile. The sweep runs under a session advisory lock (LockedMaintenanceSweep) and queues nothing while an upgrade is queued or running. failMinorUpgrade resumes the poolers and finishes the run, and the sweep finishes any run left unfinished without an operation, resuming its poolers first. The admin's Upgrade now queues the same operation and waits for it. TestMaintenanceSweepTakesALock, TestMinorUpgradeIsAnExclusiveOperation, TestSharedMinorUpgradeWaitsForItsProjects and TestMinorUpgradeOnFailAndCrash cover it.

    High availability#

    An HA project runs two Patroni members on nodes in different failure domains, with Patroni's state in its region's three-member etcd cluster. Patroni decides who leads; xenibase-server follows the leader and moves the pooler route.

    The etcd cluster and its CA#

    Each region has its own cluster, so its failover depends only on its own machines (V3.1 §3.1). ha.Setup takes three distinct healthy nodes of one region in three failure domains, refuses while any etcd setup or replacement is pending anywhere, and has each agent run etcd:v3.6.5 as a new cluster with a random token. Health is refreshed every 30 seconds; Ready, checked before HA or a replica is added, wants three members with a majority healthy.

    The etcd CA is separate from the agent CA, so neither's certificates pass for the other's. LoadCA creates it once under an advisory lock (P-256, 20 years, key sealed with the master key). Members get 5-year server-and-client certificates, and each HA instance a client certificate patroni:<instance>. Etcd checks client certificates on both ports but has no per-cluster authorisation: every Patroni scope sits under /xenibase/ and any certificate from the CA can write any key. Isolation between projects rests on tenants never getting a shell or superuser in a member container, whose environment holds the key.

    Replace swaps a member: a dead one is removed first so the other two keep a quorum, a live one (a drained node) only after the new one joins. MoveToRegionEtcd moves a project whose state is still in the home region's cluster: it removes the standby, restarts the leader on the new cluster under a pooler pause, and builds a new standby, so the project has none until the end.

    Patroni members#

    An HA instance stays one row that follows its leader: node_id, leader_member and the addresses are the leader's. Each member is a container keyed by its own ID in instance_members, and the first member's ID is the instance's (leaderKey). memberSpec is the plain spec plus a Patroni block: the scope, the region's etcd endpoints, the instance's etcd certificate, the replication and REST passwords and synchronous mode. The agent writes the configuration:

    Turning HA on and off#

    EnableHA needs a running instance, its region's etcd ready, and a node from standbyNode: healthy, dedicated-capable, in the region, holding no member, in another failure domain, with the fewest instances. Unlike placeDedicated it does not check that the size fits there. runHAEnable then creates xenibase_replicator and the Patroni secret, recreates the container under Patroni on the same data with the poolers frozen (about 4 seconds; on failure back to a plain container), starts the standby from the newest base backup (pg_basebackup as fallback), waits until it streams, and adds the SLA probe login. A standby that never joins is removed. Turning HA off removes the standby and leaves Patroni with one member, so turning it on again needs no restart. With HA on, node moves, demotion, major upgrades and stop or restart are refused.

    The HA watcher: failover and routing#

    Patroni promotes the standby when the leader's 20-second lease expires and the standby is under 1 MB behind. The route is the server's job: RunHAWatcher takes a session advisory lock on a connection of its own, and while it holds it polls every instance under Patroni once a second; the other servers try for the lock every 5 seconds. clusterViews asks every member's Patroni for the cluster, and watchOne decides:

    The leader is the running one the members that answer list (agreedLeader; the one most of them list when they disagree). A leader the server cannot reach is still the leader while the other members list it, so a fault between the server and one node changes nothing. Only when every member that answers lists no running leader, for two polls, are the routes frozen so clients queue: Patroni has dropped the leader and is electing another. When no member answers at all the poolers are left as they are. A new leader is written onto the row and the poolers synced (routeTo), a failover_events row records the outage, and the poolers resume. The old primary rejoins through pg_rewind. Writes come back 17 to 20 seconds after the primary's node dies in the tests. When etcd loses its quorum, failsafe mode keeps a primary that reaches every member serving, and no failover happens until the quorum returns; ensureFailsafe turns it on for clusters made before it was the default.

    Spec and code differ

    V3 §2.2 fences with "Patroni's watchdog plus the leader lease". Containers have no watchdog device, so Patroni runs with watchdog: off and the lease alone fences (decision M19 #6): a primary whose Patroni hangs while Postgres runs is stopped by nothing, and only the poolers' following the lease keeps traffic off it. The spec also puts etcd on the control node and moves archiving with Patroni callbacks; the code runs a cluster per region on tenant nodes and needs no callbacks, as Postgres archives only on a primary.

    Resolved

    The watcher used to pause a healthy project whenever the control plane lost sight of its primary: "no leader" included the leader's REST API not answering xenibase-server within 2 seconds, twice, so a fault between the server and one node froze every HA project led there although Patroni, etcd and the poolers were fine. With two servers on one metadata database each ran the watcher with its own paused flag and switchover mutex, so one server's partial view paused poolers only it would resume, and the other recorded a "failover" for the first's switchover. Now the poolers pause only when the members that answer agree there is no running leader (agreedLeader), and nothing changes when none answers. The watcher runs on one server at a time under the advisory lock haWatchLockKey, held by a session on a connection of its own and checked before every poll; a server whose connection fails resumes the poolers it paused, and the next holder's first poll resumes the rest. A switchover marks the instance (switchover_started_at, migration 00073) for as long as it runs, wherever its operation runs, and the watcher leaves a marked instance alone for up to 5 minutes. TestWatcherWaitsForPatroniToDropTheLeader, TestWatcherSkipsAMarkedSwitchover and TestHAWatcherRunsOnOneServer cover it.

    Switchover and synchronous replication#

    switchOver holds the instance's watcher mutex and marks the instance for the watcher on whichever server holds the lock, picks the least-lagging streaming standby that is not a replica (with synchronous replication, the synchronous standby, waiting up to 30 seconds for one), freezes the poolers, calls Patroni's /switchover, waits for the candidate to lead, routes and resumes. The old primary stops cleanly first, so nothing is lost; about 2 seconds of pause. Synchronous replication patches synchronous_mode in Patroni's configuration; without it a failover can lose up to 1 MB of acknowledged commits.

    The SLA probes#

    HA projects carry 99.9% monthly availability of the pooler endpoint. ensureProbe creates a login <db>_sla with only CONNECT and a limit of 5 connections. Every minute SLATick connects through each project's pooled URL and runs SELECT 1 within five seconds; with a status page it also pushes the targets to xenibase-status and pulls its per-minute results, both signed. A minute is unavailable when every vantage point that probed in it failed. Minutes while the project is not active or its organisation is suspended are excluded, as are minutes inside maintenance announced to the project 72 hours before them (ApplyMaintenanceExclusions, over the last six hours on every tick).

    Spec and code differ

    V3 §2.7 counts a minute unavailable "if the probe fails from two vantage points". The code needs only every vantage point that probed to fail, so without a status page one failed internal probe makes a minute unavailable (decision M19 #11).

    Failure domains and regions#

    A failure domain is what fails with a node: a rack, a host, a power feed. Separated decides whether two nodes can fail together. A recorded domain wins and a node without one counts as alone; otherwise two Hetzner servers are apart only inside the same spread placement group, and a node with neither is its own domain. The rule binds an HA pair (standbyNode refuses), a region's etcd members (setup and replacement refuse) and a region's pooler pair (a warning); read replicas never take over, so they are exempt. Changing a domain moves nothing: faildomain.Check lists the groups that now break it, for a banner and a failure_domain alert.

    A region groups nodes, a pooler pair with its own hostname (pooler hosts), a storage target and a copy target. Placement, standbys, promotions and demotions stay in the project's region. A hidden region's launch checks (Readiness) block opening it without a healthy node, with etcd that is not three members in three domains, or with a pair sharing a domain.

    Read replicas#

    A read replica is a member tagged nofailover and nosync: it streams from whichever member leads, is never promoted and never holds up a commit. A project may have two. runCreateReplica first puts a plain instance under Patroni (the same restart as HA), then builds the member from the newest base backup on a healthy node holding no member, in the project's region or, without data residency, another. Every replica of an instance publishes on one port, 20000 + fnv32(instance) % 10000, because PgBouncer takes one port for a host list. Moves, demotions, major upgrades and the regional etcd move are refused while a project has replicas.

    The pooler renders <db>_ro for such a project: the same logins, each server connection started with SET default_transaction_read_only = on, balanced across the replicas in rotation in the pooler's region, else all in rotation, else the primary (replicaHosts). Read-only is a session default the client can change, not a permission. On every watcher poll checkReplicas measures each replica's lag as how long ago the leader was first seen past the position the replica has not replayed, so a replica that stops replaying lags even while the leader is idle. Over 10 seconds, or not streaming, takes it out of rotation; under half that brings it back.

    Per-replica standby settings#

    Each replica has its own hot_standby_feedback and one delay for both max_standby_streaming_delay and max_standby_archive_delay; the primary and standbys keep Postgres's defaults.

    They reach the replica twice: in memberSpec's local parameters, so a recreated container starts with them, and through UpdateReplicaSettings, which stores them and, on a streaming replica, runs ALTER SYSTEM and a reload and reads back what the server runs with. The values can only be on, off or <n>s, checked before quoting. The watcher re-confirms them every 5 minutes (30 seconds after a failure), which also covers a replica rebuilt from a base backup with the primary's postgresql.auto.conf.

    Detaching a replica#

    DetachReplica turns a streaming replica into a new dedicated project while the source runs on. The new instance takes the member's ID, so container and volume keep their names. ensureDetached deletes the member row, recreates the container as a plain instance with the source's superuser, promotes it with pg_promote, resets primary_conninfo, the slot and the standby settings, and renames the database and owner as a restore does. A failure removes the new project and the replica.

    Moves#

    A node move (logical_move), a major upgrade (Postgres versions and upgrades), a promotion and a demotion all copy through one engine. A node move to another region's node is a region move. Each holds the project in a non-active status, which keeps other operations off it, for two attempts. Move refuses HA, replicas, the same node, a region the project's data residency or a hidden region's early access forbids, and a region move while the project has stored files (File storage). A shared project goes into the target node's shared cluster of the same major; a dedicated one gets a new instance of the same size.

    The copy#

    runMove first checks where the project is: already on the target means the cutover committed and only finishMove is left. Otherwise a second attempt first unfreezes the source, in case the first froze it, and it creates a new target instance, and prepareTarget creates the database and every login with the same SCRAM verifiers (owner, members, integrator roles, roles the owner made, NOLOGIN stand-ins for roles grants name); a second attempt first clears the first's replication objects and recreates the database. copyForMove then:

    1. Preflight (Preflight): wal_level=logical, a free slot and WAL sender, a target major no older, no large objects or unlogged tables, the extensions available on the target. Any blocker falls back to dump and restore inside the freeze, recorded as fallback_reason.
    2. Schema: pg_dump --schema-only | pg_restore through the target node's agent, owners kept.
    3. Replication (Setup): REPLICA IDENTITY FULL on tables without a primary key, a marker table on both sides, an event trigger refusing tenants' DDL, a REPLICATION login xenibase_move_<op> (agents admit it only from XENIBASE_AGENT_MOVE_ALLOW), a publication FOR ALL TABLES, and a subscription with disable_on_error and, at the same major, binary.
    4. Catch up (WaitCaughtUp): every table copied, then under 1 MB behind for 30 seconds.
    5. Freeze (freeze): owner and member logins NOLOGIN, the poolers frozen, those roles' and the console's sessions ended.
    6. Cutover, within 30 seconds: the marker below, then each used sequence set to the source's value plus 1,000 steps, then exact row counts on up to 20 tables of at most 16 MB.

    A dump-mode move copies with pg_dump | pg_restore inside the freeze and compares every table and sequence, so its pause grows with size. A logical move's does not: 115 ms at 1 GB and 135 ms at 3 GB under continuous commits, none lost (TestMoveUnderLoad).

    Spec and code differ

    Decision M18 #5 says missing extensions on the target block the move. In the code they are one more preflight blocker and every caller allows the dump fallback, so the move freezes writes, fails at CREATE EXTENSION and rolls back: a pause and a failed move instead of a refusal.

    The switch, and how the URL stays the same#

    MoveCutOver points the project at the target. Nothing in a connection string names an instance (the pooler host, database name, role and password all stay), so once finishMove re-renders the route and resumes, the held clients carry on against the target. A region move changes the hostname to the new region's, and keeps the old region in forward_region with forward_until 30 days ahead; while that is in the future the pooler sync also renders the project into the old region's configuration (served), so the old hostname reaches the new instance until the first sync after it.

    finishMove is idempotent and is also the rollback after the commit. It sets the project active, keeps the source for 48 hours (a shared copy read-only, a dedicated instance stopped) for DropRetired to remove, removes the replication objects on both sides in a deferred cleanupMove, and takes the target's first base backup, where its point-in-time window starts. Before the commit, failMove removes the replication objects, unfreezes the source, sets the project active, and destroys the new instance or drops the partial copy. If the source's logins cannot be given back, the poolers still resume and the target still goes, but the project keeps its status for the sweep below to finish.

    Resolved

    A retry after the freeze used to copy everything again with the source still frozen: only the rollback, after the last attempt, unfroze. A transient error between freeze and the cutover commit, or a crash, lost lease or deploy in that window, started attempt two with the logins NOLOGIN and the poolers paused, and in dump mode the project stayed unreachable for a second whole copy. Now runMove, runPromote and runDemote call thawRetry on any attempt after the first that finds the project not yet cut over: the logins get LOGIN back and the poolers resume, so the source serves while the attempt copies again, until its own freeze (TestRetryUnfreezesTheSource).

    Resolved

    A rollback that could not reach the source used to leave the project frozen and stuck. unfreeze opened a connection to the source first and, if that failed (often why the move failed), returned before resuming the poolers, and failMove before setting the project active; Runner.fail logged "rollback incomplete" and never retried, so the project stayed moving, NOLOGIN and paused until someone repaired it by hand. Promotion and demotion shared this. Now thaw resumes the poolers whether or not the logins could be given back, and the rollback still removes the target; only the project's status stays as it was, which keeps other operations off it, and the operation fails with the reason in its log. Every minute, beside the reaper, RepairStuckMoves takes each project in moving, promoting, demoting or upgrading with no queued or running operation, gives its logins LOGIN back, resumes its poolers and sets it active once its instance answers, and the alerts raise project_stuck for one still frozen after 10 minutes (TestFailedRollbackResumesAndIsRepaired).

    Resolved

    Replication objects a cleanup could not remove used to stay for ever. cleanupMove is best effort, logical.Cleanup skips a side it cannot open, and nothing else looked for xenibase_move_ objects; with no instance setting max_slot_wal_keep_size, an orphaned slot kept WAL until the disk filled (on a shared cluster, for every tenant there), and the event trigger kept refusing the tenant's DDL. Now every hour SweepMoveLeftovers visits each running instance and shared cluster on a healthy node and, in the databases that belong to Xenibase projects, lists the move objects (logical.FindLeftovers), then checks each against the operations: a subscription, publication, inactive slot or login named after an operation no longer queued or running is dropped, and the DDL block and move schema go from a database that no such operation is moving to or from that instance. Checking after listing keeps a move that starts meanwhile clear of it. Slot WAL is also capped: a quarter of a dedicated instance's volume, at least 1 GB, and 10 GB on an agent-run shared cluster, applied when an instance is next created or recreated (TestSweepMoveLeftovers, TestSlotWALIsCapped).

    Resolved

    A region move used to leave the WAL archive in the old region. The target's archive is placed once, when it first runs, and it was placed from the project as it was before the cutover, so regionTarget picked the old region's bucket and the moved project's WAL and base backups stayed there for the instance's life. Now placeArchive asks for the target by the region of the instance's node, where the project will be once the cutover commits. A project with its own storage target keeps it, and a data-residency project never leaves its region, so neither changes (TestPlaceArchiveFollowsTheNodesRegion).

    Promotion and demotion#

    Promotion (runPromote) moves a shared project, not a branch, onto a new dedicated instance in its region. The wizard's estimate is 5 seconds for a logical copy, or 5 seconds plus the size at 40 MiB/s for dump and restore. The target is the project as it will be: the same role, verifier and database name, dedicated limits, timeouts kept, the console read-only. CutOverProject switches instance, tier and settings in one statement, the shared copy is kept read-only for 48 hours, and the instance takes its first base backup.

    Demotion refuses HA and replicas, and preflight runs seven checks: size against the shared storage limits, extensions outside the shared allow-list, roles beyond the project's own (integrator roles block), the allowance released, last week's peak connections (a warning), settings the copy drops (a warning), and a shared cluster of the same major in the region with room for the size plus 20%. They run at preflight, at queue time and again in runDemote. After the cutover finishDemotion takes a logical backup (point-in-time recovery ends) and stops the dedicated instance, destroyed 48 hours later; its WAL-G archive stays for the base backups still under it.

    Spec and code differ

    V1 §6.6 freezes with ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false and verifies every table's rows. The code uses NOLOGIN, which leaves pg_dump working (decision M5 #2), and a logical copy counts only small tables, trusting the marker (M18 #3). V3 §2.3 keeps every source read-only for 48 hours; a dedicated source is stopped instead.

    Failure handling#

    What failsWhat happens
    The HA primary's nodePoolers paused after two missed polls; Patroni promotes the standby when the lease expires (if under 1 MB behind); the route moves and the poolers resume. The old primary rejoins with pg_rewind.
    The standby's nodeNothing for clients; synchronous mode drops to asynchronous rather than block commits.
    One etcd member, or the quorumOne: no effect; replace it. The quorum: failsafe mode keeps primaries serving, and no failover until it returns.
    xenibase-serverPatroni fails over without it, but the route waits for a server. Another server takes the watcher lock once the stopped one's session ends, and on its first poll it resumes every HA project's poolers. A server whose lock connection fails resumes the poolers it paused before it stops watching.
    A replica that lags or stopsOut of _ro past 10 s, back under 5 s; with none in rotation the route reads from the primary.
    A move before its cutoverTwo attempts, the second starting with the source unfrozen, then failMove restores the source and destroys the target; a source it cannot reach is repaired by the sweep once it answers.
    A move after its cutoverOnly finishMove runs again; the source is kept 48 hours.
    Replication or the marker failsdisable_on_error stops the subscription and the attempt fails; a marker missing after 30 s is permanent and rolls back.
    A resize or minor upgradeThe old size goes back on the row; a failed minor upgrade is recorded and retried at a later sweep.
