    • internal/freetier/sweep.go
    • internal/store/queries/billing.sql
    • and 4 more

    Billing turns recorded usage into invoices, posts every movement of money to a double-entry ledger, and collects from each organisation's wallet at the wallet provider. Prices are in US dollars and money moves in naira: an invoice is converted when it is issued, at a rate frozen on it. Three neighbours share the page because they spend or save money for the platform: the Free tier pauses and archives idle projects, capacity automation buys and deletes servers, and cost attribution says what each organisation costs. Legal documents record what organisations agreed to.

    • billing6,945 linesXenibase's billing core (V3 §3): price books, billing accounts, the double-entry ledger, rating, invoices and credit notes, the forecast and spend controls.
    • freetier745 linesPauses and archives inactive Free projects (V3 §4): a Free project with no client connections for 7 days is paused (its database refuses connections and its pooler route points at the waker); one paused for 90 days is archived (a verified f…
    • costs1,019 linesAttributes what the infrastructure costs to the organisations that use it (V3 §5.4), keeps exchange rates, and computes margins per organisation and plan for the platform admin's dashboard (§7.2).
    • capacity1,727 linesAdds and removes database nodes by itself (V3 §5.2, §5.3): it watches each region's shared disk and dedicated headroom, proposes a server when a threshold trips, provisions proposals within the monthly infrastructure budget (others wait for…
    • legal282 linesKeeps Xenibase's legal documents (V3 §7.3) that organisations accept: the service level agreement, the data processing agreement, and an organisation's own order form.

    Every loop here runs on every xenibase-server without a leader lock: billing.Run every 10 minutes, capacity.Run every 30 seconds. They rely on idempotency keys, unique indexes and row locks rather than on running once.

    Money and currencies#

    No amount passes through a float between a usage record and an invoice (decision M20 #1). Money is int64 in minor units; unit prices, quantities and rates are Dec, a math/big.Rat carried in JSON as a string. Each invoice line is rounded once, half away from zero:

    AmountUnit
    Price book fees and unit pricesCents of USD (fractions allowed), or kobo for an NGN book
    Invoices, ledger, payments, credit notes, budget, spend capKobo; invoices keep the dollar figures beside them (usd_*)
    Infrastructure costs; the capacity budgetThe cost's own currency as fractional float64; minor units of the budget's currency

    A platform with a wallet provider starts on DefaultPrices in dollars; without one there is no rate, so it starts on DefaultPricesNGN. Both currencies have two decimals, so kobo per cent is naira per dollar (FXQuote.Naira).

    Spec and code differ

    V3 §3.3 prices in kobo. Prices moved to dollars with the wallet provider (migration 00051, docs/billing.md); what moves stays in kobo.

    Price books, plans and accounts#

    A price book is one JSON document per version (Prices): the currency, each plan's monthly and annual fee, quota plan, allowances and unit prices, the dedicated hourly rates, and the add-ons. Validate requires free, pro and team, a Free plan without fee or unit prices, no negative prices and premiums of at most 500%. Publish needs an effective date at least 30 days ahead (except the first book) and emails each affected organisation what changes; the price_book_frozen trigger refuses changes to a published row. Reprice moves organisations to the book in effect, except grandfathered ones and annual terms, which move at renewal.

    Dedicated instances, HA standbys (plus the HA premium) and read replicas are priced per vCPU-, RAM- and disk-hour whatever the plan; PITR and retention add-ons by the hour while set; a region premium as a percentage of a project's hardware lines there (regionPremium, V4.1 §4.3).

    Account creates an organisation's billing_accounts row on first need, on the current book. It holds the plan and term, the mode, the book and grandfathering, business details, WHT applicability, payment terms, budget, spend cap and forecast, the dunning state, the wallet id and the debit consent. Owners and billing members see it, admins do not (Identity, organisations and access). Prepaid, the V3 mode of daily deductions from a credit balance (DeductPrepaid), is refused for an organisation with a wallet (switchMode).

    The ledger#

    Every money movement is a Txn: a key, a source, and two or more entries whose debits equal their credits.

    AccountHoldsMoves
    receivableWhat the organisation owesDr on issue; Cr by payments, wallet debits, credit applied, credit notes, WHT
    wallet_balanceIts wallet at the provider, by Xenibase's booksCr on a verified deposit; Dr on a wallet debit
    credit_balanceOverpayments, credit on paid invoices, prepaid fundsDr when applied or refunded
    wht_receivableTax withheld, awaiting its certificateDr when a payment is short by exactly the expected WHT
    revenue:*, vat_payableRevenue per plan or line (dedicated, ha, addons, messages) and VAT owedCr on issue; Dr by credit notes
    cash:*, fees:*Money received (cash:iswallet deposits, cash:bank manual payments) and feesDr on receipt; Cr by refunds

    Post validates, then inserts each entry under the idempotency key <key>#<n> in the caller's transaction, so an invoice and its posting commit together. A key already posted with the same number of entries is a no-op; anything else is an error. The database holds the invariants whatever the code does:

    Check adds the M27 audit (BillingAuditProblems): each issued invoice's transaction carries its total and VAT, its arithmetic and allocations agree, statuses agree with what is owed, credit notes and payments have their transactions, and each receivable equals what open invoices owe. It does not compare wallet_balance with the provider; the nightly reconciliation does.

    Usage and rating#

    RecordUsage takes an advisory lock, records each completed hour since its watermark (redoing the last), each completed day of backup storage, and upserts usage_records, so a rerun changes nothing; rows older than 90 days roll up to days. Invoicing waits for the same watermark (usageRecordedThrough). Plan metrics (PlanMetrics: storage, backups, branch hours, transfer, webhook deliveries, job runs and the backend services) are rated above the plan's allowance; dedicated, HA, replica and add-on hours per project; SMS and WhatsApp codes at the provider's kobo cost plus a margin, in kobo even on a dollar book (nativeNaira). Branch storage, webhook retries and replica hours are not charged on their own.

    rate splits the month at applied plan changes, puts each day's usage in its segment, and rates each segment against its plan's allowance scaled by its days:

    Then come the per-project lines, the plan-change lines as stored, and the next month's fee in advance. For a dollar book, convert turns each line's cents into kobo and computes VAT and the expected WHT on the kobo subtotal.

    Plan changes. ChangePlan treats a higher monthly fee, or any move to annual, as an upgrade applied at once; anything else waits for the period's end unless immediately. Prorate counts days, the day of the change on the new plan: Pro → Team on 13 October (19 of 31 days) is −$6.13 and +$24.52. The lines are stored with the change and land on that month's invoice; setPlan also sets the quota plan unless the admin chose another.

    Invoices and credit notes#

    One invoice per organisation and month (UNIQUE (org_id, period_start)). Invoicing drafts the current month on its last day and handles the previous one once the watermark has passed midnight on the 1st:

    Draft re-rates a draft and replaces its lines. IssueDue does nothing until the admin turns automatic issue on; then it issues every unheld draft of the past month and earlier ones (DraftsDue), stopping for the run at the first stale rate or provider outage. Issue, in one transaction, converts a dollar draft at a fresh rate (convertDraft, the whole quote kept in invoices.fx), takes the year's next number XB-YYYY-NNNNNN from a counter row (NextBillingNumber, so a rollback gives the number back), freezes both parties' details, posts invoiceTxn (Dr receivable, Cr revenue per line and VAT) and applies any credit held. After commit it emails the contacts and debits the wallet if consented. PDFs are rendered on request from the frozen invoice (InvoicePDF). VAT (7.5%) and WHT (5%) are settings.

    CreditNote is admin-only: an amount before VAT, VAT at the invoice's rate, at most the invoice's total across its notes. creditNoteTxn debits revenue in proportion to the invoice's lines and VAT, and credits what is still owed, the rest to credit_balance.

    Immutability is in the queries

    Unlike price books and the ledger, issued invoices have no trigger. Every query that writes an invoice or its lines (UpdateDraftInvoice, SetDraftLineNaira, DeleteInvoiceLines, IssueInvoice) requires status = 'draft'; after issue only settlement columns change.

    Resolved

    Invoicing used to write billing.invoiced_through whatever DraftAll and IssueDue returned, and monthDone then skipped the month: a draft refused for a stale rate, an outage or a database error stayed a draft until the admin issued it, and an organisation whose rating failed got none. The month is now marked done only when DraftAll drafted every organisation, so a failed rating is drafted again on the next run; issuing is no longer part of it, and every run (once the watermark has passed the 1st) issues the unheld drafts of that month and earlier ones. A stale rate on the first run and a fresh one later now issues the draft, as docs/billing.md says. While any is left, from the 2nd, the status page shows "Last month's invoices are late" (Health, which counts earlier months too).

    Spec and code differ

    V3 §3.6 issues drafts automatically on the 1st. Automatic issue is off until the admin turns it on (decision M20 #10).

    The rate. Quote asks the wallet provider for USD→NGN. A strict quote, for issuing, refuses one whose fetched_at is older than fx_max_age_hours (4 hours), because the provider keeps answering with its last rate when its feed fails. Drafts and estimates reuse a quote for two minutes and accept any age. The provider sets the spread; the quote on the invoice is the only record of it.

    Wallet debits#

    Each organisation's money sits in its own wallet at the wallet provider, funded by transfer to a permanent virtual account (EnsureWallet: tier 2, a director's BVN forwarded and not kept). A verified deposit is posted Dr cash:iswallet, Cr wallet_balance, and settles nothing (recordPayment). With an owner's consent to the current terms (AcceptDebitTerms), the wallet is debited on issue, on each deposit, on dunning retries and for what is already owed; without it, on Pay from wallet (PayInvoiceFromWallet). chargeInvoiceFromWallet:

    1. Resolves any earlier attempt that got no answer by its key; while one is unresolved, stops.
    2. Reads what the invoice owes and the wallet's available balance. Short is a decline: all or nothing, and dunning starts.
    3. In one transaction, locks the account and the invoice, reads what is owed again (nothing now ends the attempt; a balance short of it is a decline) and inserts a payment_intents row for that amount with a fresh key; a partial unique index allows one pending wallet debit per invoice (payment_intents_one_wallet_debit).
    4. Transfers the intent's amount to Xenibase's operating wallet with the invoice number as narration; a 200 is final.
    5. settleWalletDebit: Dr wallet_balance, Cr receivable, and Cr credit_balance for anything no longer owed.
    Resolved

    A debit whose answer was lost used to be booked once the provider called its request terminal, whatever the request's status, so a transfer that ended failed marked the invoice paid with no money moved. Both this branch and resolveWalletIntent now read the status: only one that says it completed (RequestState.Succeeded: completed, succeeded, successful) is settled. One that ended without moving money (failed, declined, reversed and the like) closes the intent as declined, posts nothing and starts dunning for an automatic debit, as a short wallet does. A terminal status nobody has written down is neither booked nor tried again: the intent stays pending, which blocks further debits of that invoice, and an error is logged for a person (docs/iswallet.md).

    Resolved

    An attempt used to read what was owed before inserting its intent, so one that was slow to read the balance could, after another attempt had inserted, transferred and settled in between, insert its own intent (nothing was pending any more) and debit again, the second amount booked as credit: one slow balance read debited ₦65,145 for a ₦32,572.50 invoice. The read that decides the amount is now made under the invoice's row lock, in the transaction that inserts the intent; a settlement takes the same lock and finishes its intent in its own transaction, so an attempt either meets the other's pending intent (the unique index refuses it) or sees what that one paid, and transfers only what is still owed, or nothing. The pending intent is the lock across the provider calls, so no advisory lock is held over them. Credit left by an over-debit before this fix pays the next invoice, but Refund still returns only manual payments: sending wallet money back needs a reverse transfer, which Xenibase does not make.

    Resolved

    DebitTermsVersion is to change with the wording so organisations "are asked again", and ConsentOf reported Current: false, but automatic debits used to check only that debit_consent_at was set, so they went on under the old wording. They now need a consent to the current version (debitsAllowed); an older one is treated as none. Pay from wallet still works, the Billing page already asks an owner to agree again ("The debit terms changed"), and each invoice's email now says the invoice won't be debited (DebitTermsChangedNotice). No separate email goes out when the wording changes.

    Webhooks, re-query and reconciliation#

    ParseWebhook requires X-iSpend-Signature to equal Sign, an HMAC-SHA256 over "<timestamp>.<body>" compared in constant time, with the timestamp within 5 minutes; otherwise 401. Only wallet.credit.posted from a va_deposit is acted on, keyed by data.txn_id, at amount_credited (net of the provider's fee).

    The body is only a hint (decision M21 #2). HandleEvent stores the event once per (provider, event id) with the outcome of processing it (a stored one is a duplicate unless it failed; then ClaimPaymentEvent takes it and it is processed again), and settleVerified reads the transaction back and attributes it by the virtual account the provider names; with none it is unmatched until the admin attributes it. Requery lists the provider's transactions for the last two hours hourly and the previous day nightly, posts what is missing, processes again every failed event of the last 30 days (retryFailedEvents) and resolves pending debits; Reconcile then compares transactions with payments and each wallet's balance with wallet_balance. Reversals are logged and ignored, as docs/iswallet.md lists under "Still open".

    Resolved

    A failure used to answer 500 "the event will be retried" while the row stayed stored, so the provider's retry was a duplicate answered 200, and a re-query's own requery:<ref> event that failed was skipped by every later one: a deposit whose verify call failed twice stayed unbooked. A stored event whose outcome is failed, or that has had no outcome for ten minutes (its processing was cut off), is now claimed and processed again, by the provider's retry, by a re-query that lists it, and by each re-query's sweep of the last 30 days' failed events; a pending verification counts as a failure, not a rejection, and an event that could not be stored is answered 500 too. Reprocessing posts nothing twice: InsertPayment records a payment once per (provider, provider_ref), in the transaction that posts its ledger entries under payment:<id>. attempts on the event counts the tries (migration 00091); the admin's event log shows what is still failed.

    Manual payments and refunds. RecordManual records a bank payment under a reference that cannot repeat, settling the named invoice, then the oldest, then credit; one short by exactly the expected WHT settles as paid_wht_pending until the certificate is uploaded. Refund returns at most what is left of a manual payment, from credit_balance, first taking it back off the invoices it settled when asked (unapply).

    Spec and code differ

    V3 §3.7 matches a transfer for the total minus WHT. With wallets a deposit settles nothing and a debit takes the full amount owed, so an organisation that deducts WHT pays it too; the match applies only to manual payments.

    Dunning, budgets and the spend cap#

    Daily runs after 01:00 UTC and ends with RunDunning. A declined automatic debit is retried on days 3, 5 and 7; a provider outage puts the retry back instead of counting it. The ladder counts from the oldest unpaid due date: day 0 overdue, 3 restricted, 7 final notice, 10 suspended, 40 deletion scheduled with 7 days' notice. Each step is claimed in dunning_steps under UNIQUE (org_id, cycle, step) before it acts. Free organisations are never suspended; the admin can hold the ladder; paying everything reverses it (Reevaluate). RefreshForecast projects the month hourly, emails at 50, 80 and 100% of the budget, and sets capped when the projected usage charges (overage, dedicated, add-ons) reach the cap.

    StateEffect
    Restricted (day 3) or suspendedNew projects, branches, dedicated creates and replicas refused (CheckBillingStanding)
    Suspended (day 10)V2 suspension, reason billing: …; dedicated projects deleted at day 47 only if delete_for_non_payment is on
    CappedNew branches, dedicated instances, replicas, HA and add-ons refused (CheckSpendCap); webhook deliveries wait; job runs skipped; the edge cuts data and storage rate limits to a quarter and refuses new transforms and realtime connections, sparing auth (gateway)

    Nothing running stops, so a dedicated instance keeps billing past the cap: the cap pauses growth, it does not limit the bill.

    Spec and code differ

    V3 §3.8 schedules paid resources for deletion on day 40; the code deletes only if the admin opted in (decision M21 #10).

    The Free tier#

    Activity is clients seen through the poolers each minute, and console use (TouchProjectsActive, which also clears the pause warning); Xenibase's own sessions bypass the poolers. Sweep wakes projects of organisations that now pay; then, only if the waker accepts a connection (WakerReachable), warns active Free shared projects idle 6 days and queues pause_project at 7 days and 24 hours after the warning (FreeProjectsIdleSince), and archive_project after 90 days paused. Archived projects get notices 30 and 7 days before a year, then are deleted (sweepArchived). Notices are claimed by conditional updates, so several servers send each once.

    runPause re-checks the plan and activity, points the route at the waker first, then sets ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false and ends the sessions. The waker (Connections: poolers and the edge) calls Wake and refuses with 08004 and "retry in about 30 seconds". runArchive takes an archive backup, which backup.Archive verifies by restoring it into a scratch database, marks the project archived and drops the database; roles stay, so runUnarchive restores it under the same connection string. A retry reuses an earlier attempt's backup, and drops the database only on one whose restore passed:

    Resolved

    A retry used to drop the database on an unverified backup: backup.Archive marked the row succeeded before verifyRestore ran, and deleted it only if verification failed and the delete worked, so after a crash during verification, or a failed delete, the next attempt found the row through BackupForOperation and went straight to DROP DATABASE … WITH (FORCE), against V3 §4.3 and decision M22 #5. Now VerifyArchive sets backups.verified_at only when the restore passed (migration 00093); runArchive verifies an earlier attempt's unverified backup again, and refuses to drop without a verified one, leaving the project paused when the operation gives up. Tests: TestArchiveRetryVerifiesAnUnverifiedBackupBeforeDropping, …KeepsTheDatabaseWhenTheBackupCannotBeVerified and TestVerifyArchiveKeepsAnUndeletableBackupUnverified.

    Resolved

    Decision M22 #2 pauses only Free projects of active organisations, re-checked when the operation runs. runPause and runArchive used to re-check activity, not the plan, so a project whose organisation upgraded after the sweep was paused or archived and then woken by the next sweep. Both now ask mayNotSleep (ProjectSleepPlan: an active organisation on the Free plan, not Unlimited, and a shared project) and skip otherwise; runArchive asks again after the backup, before the drop, and a pause retried on a project an earlier attempt paused wakes it. FreeProjectsPausedSince now skips suspended organisations too. Tests: TestPauseRechecksThePlan and TestArchiveRechecksThePlanBeforeTheDrop.

    Abuse limits on open signup (Turnstile, three accounts a day per IP, verified email, TOTP, one personal organisation) are on Identity, organisations and access.

    Cost attribution and margins#

    Attribute divides each UTC day's cost among organisations, in each cost's currency: a node's monthly price over the month's days, by dedicated instances' vCPU share (standbys as ha), the rest to its shared projects half by storage and half by connection-hours, unused as idle; edge nodes by API requests and realtime minutes; storage, transfer and messages by use; floating IPs and overheads to nobody. Rates for costs are naira per unit, entered by hand with history (RatesAt), separate from the provider's invoice rate. Margins sets a month's cost at today's rate and at each day's (the difference is FX erosion) against what it earns (earned).

    Reporting only

    Attribution's float64 moves no money. Margin revenue re-rates the month at the organisation's current book and today's rate rather than reading the issued invoice, so after a repricing a past month differs from what was invoiced.

    Capacity automation#

    Evaluate runs hourly per region and tier, skipping a tier with a node already provisioning: shared disk projected past 70% within 14 days (a week's slope per node); no healthy dedicated host with room for the largest profile; edges above 70% CPU in 11 of the hour's 12 buckets. propose prices a server from the provider's catalog and inserts a proposal; a partial unique index allows one open proposal per region and tier. It starts by itself only with a provider that creates servers, automatic provisioning on, and room in the budget, checked and started in one transaction under an advisory lock (LockCapacityBudget):

    The budget is zero by default, so nothing is bought until one is set; otherwise the proposal waits for Approve, behind step-up auth (decision M24 #6). A dedicated create that finds no host calls HostFor, which joins the region's proposal and waits for its node, or answers 409 capacity_pending_approval.

    Resolved

    The budget used to be checked one proposal at a time: it summed existing nodes only, and a started proposal has no node until its operation runs proposalNode, so one Evaluate over several regions and tiers, or simultaneous HostFor calls, saw the same headroom and all started (nodes costing 1,500, a budget of 3,000 and four 1,000 proposals: 5,500 a month). Now BudgetCostTotals adds approved and provisioning proposals whose node isn't counted yet, in one statement so a proposal getting its node meanwhile counts once, and propose checks, inserts and starts under the advisory lock, which Approve's start takes too; a waiter gives up after 30 seconds. TestBudgetCountsStartedProposals runs that scenario concurrently, through propose and HostFor: one starts, three wait.

    runProvision creates the node with a one-time token, the server with the token in its cloud-init (found again by label on a retry), waits 20 minutes for the agent, creates a shared node's cluster and puts the node into service. On failure failProvision deletes the server and node if nothing runs there. Drain queues a move per project; advanceMoves runs one at a time through the zero-downtime move (Dedicated instances, HA and moves), skipping HA, paused and archived projects. Rebalance proposes up to ten moves a week from the fullest to the emptiest shared node while their disk use differs by more than 15%. sweepEmpty deletes a provider's server that has held nothing for 24 hours (NodeOccupancy: projects, archived ones included, dedicated instances, kept move copies, HA and etcd members), unless marked keep, over two sweeps: the first takes the node out of placement, the second, after a grace period, counts again and deletes.

    Resolved

    The empty-node sweep used to destroy the server before checking again: occupancy was read once per sweep, then deleteNode deleted the server, retired its shared clusters, and only then called RemoveNode, whose instance check passed because the clusters were just retired; placement did not exclude empty nodes and prefers the emptiest cluster, so a project placed in between lost its database. Now startRetire counts again under the node's row lock and sets lifecycle retiring (migration 00094), which every placement query excludes, and provision.Create holds the node's row FOR SHARE until the project is recorded (LockNodeForPlacement), choosing again if it finds the node retiring. After RetireGrace (10 minutes), finishRetire counts once more under the lock and either puts the node back as it was or retires its clusters, deletes the server, and removes the node, in that order. Tests: TestEmptySweepPutsBackANodeSomethingWasPlacedOn, TestEmptySweepDeletesTheServerLast and TestPlacementWaitsForTheEmptyNodeSweep.

    Spec and code differ

    V3 §5.3 evens out disk and CPU; the rebalancer compares disk only.

    Legal documents#

    Each person accepts the terms, privacy notice and AUP through the terms gate (Identity, organisations and access). Each organisation accepts the SLA, the DPA and its own order form: Publish numbers versions per kind and organisation, the latest is in effect, and Accept takes only that version, recording the owner and IP once. A plan change may carry accept_legal (ChangeOrgPlan), and Billing shows a banner while anything is outstanding.

    Spec and code differ

    Paid plans work without accepting the SLA and DPA (decision M23 #9): V3 §7.3's acceptance is a record, not a gate.

    Failure handling#

    What failsWhat happens
    A server dies while issuingNumber, totals, posting and credit applied are one transaction and roll back together; email and debit come after commit.
    The rate is stale at issueThe draft stays a draft, the run stops issuing, and the next run (10 minutes later) tries every unheld draft again.
    Usage recording is behindThe previous month is not issued until the watermark passes midnight on the 1st.
    The wallet provider is downThe attempt is recorded "provider unavailable", not counted against the customer, and retried by the daily dunning; the status page shows billing degraded.
    A transfer gets no clear answerIts key is looked up: a 404 allows another attempt; a non-terminal state stays pending for the re-query; a terminal one is booked only if it completed, is a decline if it failed, and otherwise stays pending for a person.
    A webhook is forged or stale401, nothing stored.
    A webhook fails to process500; the provider's retry processes it again, as do the hourly re-queries for 30 days; reconciliation lists what is missing meanwhile.
    The waker is downwaker_down fires and the sweep neither pauses nor archives; dashboard resume still works.
    Archive verification fails or is cut shortThe backup is deleted (or, if that fails, left unverified and tested again by the retry); the database is dropped only on a verified backup, and when the operation gives up the project stays paused.
    A new server never joinsAfter 20 minutes the server is deleted, the node removed and the proposal failed.
    Several servers run a loopLedger keys, dunning_steps, one invoice per period and one open proposal per region and tier make the second run a no-op; a wallet debit reads what is owed under the invoice's lock as it records its attempt, and a capacity budget check holds a lock until its proposal has started.

    Part F · Running it

    Operations

    Running Xenibase: deployment bundles, alerts, metrics, logs, the status page and incidents, and support.

    Checked against ef67bfb · 2026-10-29No changes to its code since

    This page is how Xenibase is installed, upgraded and watched once it runs: the Docker Compose bundle and its scripts, the images for the other machines, what an operator must keep off the server, the alerts and how they reach someone, the metrics, the logs, the separately hosted status page with its incidents, and the support desk. The services these watch are on their own pages and are linked, not repeated.

    • alerts1,203 linesRaises alerts for the conditions of spec §8.8 and delivers them to a webhook and, optionally, by email.
    • metrics685 linesSamples project and node metrics into metric_points, downsamples them, and serves series and the Prometheus exposition (spec §8.7).
    • logging16 linesBuilds the process-wide slog logger.
    • statuspage2,187 linesXenibase-status (V3 §2.6): a public status page that runs away from Xenibase, probes it from outside, takes signed heartbeats and incidents from xenibase-server, opens and resolves incidents by itself, keeps 90 days of history, and ema…
    • statusapi348 linesThe contract between xenibase-server and the separately hosted status service, xenibase-status (V3 §2.6): signed heartbeats for the components the status service can't probe from outside, and incidents the platform admin posts in Xenibase.
    • incidents1,073 linesXenibase's side of the status page (V3 §2.6): the platform admin's incidents, pushed to xenibase-status with a signature, and the heartbeat that reports the components xenibase-status can't probe from outside.
    • support962 linesXenibase's ticket system (V3 §7.1): tickets opened from the dashboard, by email to the support address, or by WhatsApp, threaded into one inbox for the support console, with response targets by plan.
    • version31 linesExposes build information injected at link time.

    The compose bundle#

    A single-host install is deploy/compose/compose.yaml (V1 §11.1), project name xenibase. Everything is on one bridge network, 172.31.250.0/24, named after XENIBASE_NETWORK (default xenibase) so the agent can attach dedicated instances to it. The services that other configuration names by address have fixed ones below .20; Docker hands out the rest from .128/25.

    ServiceImageAddress and portsWhat it does
    caddycaddy:2, or a build with a DNS plugin.10; 80 and 443 publishedTLS for the web UI and, with backend services on, the wildcard API domain. Forwards other hosts' ACME challenges to the server.
    xenibase-serverxenibase:local.11; 8080 inside, the waker on 6435The control plane. Trusts X-Forwarded-For from Caddy's address only (XENIBASE_TRUSTED_PROXIES). Health check: xenibase-server -healthcheck, a GET of /healthz.
    pooler-session, pooler-txedoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.1-p0.12, .13; 5432 and 6543 publishedThe two PgBouncers (Connections: poolers and the edge). They read deploy/pgbouncer/*.ini and the files the server writes into the shared pooler-config volume.
    xenibase-agentxenibase-agent:local.14The local node's agent, as root with the Docker socket, because dedicated instances are its sibling containers (Nodes and agents). Registers itself with AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN.
    metadata-dbpostgres:18not publishedThe metadata database, SCRAM for TCP logins.
    shared-pgpostgres:18not publishedThe shared cluster, with V1 §11.2's tuning for an 8 GB host, wal_level=logical for moves, and shared-pg-hba.conf: SCRAM from .11 to .14 only, and each move's own login from the subnet.
    xenibase-edgexenibase-edge:localdynamic; 8443 insideBackend services' gateway, in the services profile, off until enable-services.sh (The data API).

    Seven named volumes hold the state, among them pooler-config (written by the server, read-only in the poolers) and agent-state (the agent's identity and pinned CA). The server runs as uid 70, PgBouncer's user, so the poolers can read the 0640 files it writes. Secrets are environment variables from deploy/compose/.env; a required one is written ${NAME:?message}, so Compose refuses to start without it. Everything optional is passed through empty, which the server reads as off. Caddyfile serves the UI, imports caddy.d/*.caddy (empty until backend services are on), and on port 80 sends other hosts' /.well-known/acme-challenge/* to the server, which gets the database hostname's certificate itself (Connections: poolers and the edge).

    install.sh#

    install.sh installs and also upgrades in place. It runs from a git checkout, because the version it stamps comes from git describe. In order:

    1. Checks for Docker and Compose v2.
    2. If there is no .env: asks for the UI hostname and ACME email (or reads them from the environment), checks both by pattern, looks up the public IP from ipify, and under umask 077 writes .env with a fresh 32-byte master key and three 24-byte passwords. An existing .env is kept as it is.
    3. Appends what later releases added to old files: AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN and XENIBASE_PUBLIC_URL.
    4. Builds the Postgres image for majors 17 and 18 (build.sh), then the server and the agent from the repository's Dockerfile with VERSION and COMMIT build arguments, and the edge too when COMPOSE_PROFILES includes services.
    5. docker compose up -d --no-build --wait, then recreates both poolers. A checkout replaces the bind-mounted .ini files with new inodes, and a running PgBouncer would keep reading the old one.
    6. Prints the URL and the first-run setup code, grepped from the server's log.

    The Dockerfile builds the web app with Node 22 and both binaries with Go 1.26 without cgo, checks that the server embeds the real UI (-require-ui), and ships the server on distroless and the agent on postgres:18 with CA roots for S3.

    upgrade.sh, and deploying from GitHub#

    upgrade.sh <tag> wraps install.sh with checks, a backup and a rollback. It first copies itself to a temporary file and re-executes from there, because git checkout replaces the script while the shell is still reading it. Exit status 0 is upgraded, 1 refused before any change, 2 failed and rolled back (or stopped with --no-rollback), 3 failed and the rollback failed too.

    1. Checks. A release tag that exists after git fetch --tags; unless --force, a clean tree and every service healthy; 10 GB free; and the tag's newest migration file not below the database's goose_db_version, so a downgrade is refused.
    2. Backup. pg_dump -Fc of the metadata database into upgrade-backups/, checked to be non-empty and to list goose_db_version, with a .meta file naming the release and schema it came from.
    3. Upgrade. git checkout the tag and run install.sh. The old containers serve while the images build.
    4. Gates. For up to UPGRADE_WAIT seconds (300), gates waits for every service to be running and healthy, xenibase-server -version to report the tag, and the schema to be at the tag's last migration. Operations that failed since the start are reported, not counted as a failure.
    5. Rollback, on any failure in steps 3 and 4:

    Each migration runs in its own transaction, so one that fails leaves the schema at the last that succeeded, and the rollback sees the version moved and restores. Since 4.1 a server also refuses a schema newer than it knows (refuseNewerSchema). There are no previous-release images to switch back to: each build retags xenibase:local, so the rollback rebuilds the old checkout, normally from Docker's cache. Only the Postgres image keeps its predecessor, tagged by minor release (build.sh, Postgres versions and upgrades).

    Risk

    A rollback throws away more than the upgrade. The dump is taken before the image build; the old server keeps writing through the build (often minutes) and the new one through up to five minutes of gates. A rollback after a migration restores the dump, so that whole window goes, and the metadata is not the only state: a project created in it keeps its database and roles on the cluster with no row, a project deleted in it comes back as a row without a database, a password changed in it no longer matches the restored verifier, and a payment webhook processed in it is lost for good. docs/deploying.md's "project data is unaffected" undersells it. Dumping after the build, with the old server stopped, would shrink the window to the migration.

    From GitHub. The Deploy workflow refuses a tag whose ci, e2e, docs-install and audit checks did not pass, waits for a reviewer of the production environment, and runs one deploy at a time (concurrency: deploy-production). Its key is restricted to the forced command deploy-ssh.sh, which accepts only upgrade <tag> [--dry-run], status and last, and runs an upgrade under nohup so a dropped connection cannot kill it half-way. make test-deploy runs both scripts against a fake docker through twelve scenarios, failed migration and failed rollback among them (upgrade_test.sh).

    The other scripts and images#

    WhatWhere it runsNotes
    enable-services.sh <api-domain> [provider]The bundle's hostTurns backend services on: needs the DNS provider's credentials already in .env (it never writes them), adds XENIBASE_EDGE_SECRET (40 random bytes) and COMPOSE_PROFILES=services, builds Caddy with the Cloudflare, deSEC or acme-dns plugin, writes caddy.d/api.caddy for *.<api-domain> with a DNS-01 challenge, starts the edge and reloads Caddy.
    preflight.shA server before installChanges nothing; PASS, WARN or FAIL for the OS, clock, DNS, ports, bucket and SMTP.
    Pooler hostA region's two edge pooler hostsThe agent in pooler mode and both PgBouncers in one container, uid 70, host networking. entrypoint.sh seeds placeholder routes, renders keepalived.conf and the .ini files, and exits when any process exits, so the peer takes the floating IP. keepalived is a second container, the only one with NET_ADMIN (Connections: poolers and the edge).
    Edge, statusA region's nodes; another providerDistroless, uid 65532. The status page's compose file puts Caddy in front and mounts status.toml and secrets/ read-only.
    PostgresEvery node with instancesThe official image at a pinned minor (17.11, 18.6), WAL-G v3.0.9 from a pinned commit, Patroni 4.1.5, hypopg and CA roots. An init script writes pg_hba.conf: SCRAM from XENIBASE_HBA_ALLOW only.

    What the operator must keep off the server#

    Three things, and the server cannot recover any of them:

    • .env, for XENIBASE_MASTER_KEY. It seals every stored credential and the derive seed (Security and tenant isolation). The generated file says so in its first line.
    • The backup key (Settings → Backup key). It decrypts every backup on platform targets, the metadata self-backups included, and never changes.
    • The bucket credentials of the default storage target, where metadata/ lives.

    With those, docs/disaster-recovery.md rebuilds a lost control node from the newest nightly metadata backup (Backups, restores and imports). The upgrade-backups/ dumps are a second, local copy taken before each upgrade. They are never pruned.

    Alerts#

    Every XENIBASE_ALERTS_INTERVAL (30 s, 1 s to 1 h), each server runs Tick: evaluate every condition, then deliver what is pending. The list is V1 §8.8's plus what later milestones added.

    KindSeverityFires when
    backup_failedcriticalThe latest finished backup or base_backup of a live project, or the latest metadata_backup, failed
    backup_overduewarningA project the scheduler backs up, older than 26 h, has no successful backup in 26 h (Backups, restores and imports)
    restore_test_failedcriticalThe latest restore test failed, per project for one run on demand, else the scheduled one
    wal_archivecriticalA dedicated project's archiver failed in the last 15 min, or a segment has waited over 15 min
    isolation_check_failedcriticalA live shared cluster's latest isolation check failed (Security and tenant isolation)
    minor_upgrade_failedcriticalA live instance's latest minor upgrade failed
    project_stuckcriticalA project frozen by a failed move, promotion, demotion or major upgrade 10 min on
    node_unreachablecriticalAn agent has not answered for 2 min (last_reachable_at)
    node_diskwarningA reachable node's data disk is over 85% full, from its last health report
    project_diskwarningA project's size sample from the last 30 min is over its disk warning
    pooler_downcriticalA local PgBouncer's admin console has not answered for 1 min
    pooler_allowlist_offcriticalA local PgBouncer is not on auth_type = hba
    pooler_config_skippedcriticalThe last pooler sync left rows out as invalid
    pooler_host_not_readycriticalA healthy edge pooler host reports not ready for 1 min
    pooler_split_braincriticalTwo hosts in one region are keepalived MASTER for 1 min
    waker_downcriticalThe waker refuses TCP for 1 min
    agent_client_certcriticalThe server's client certificate for agents has under 3 days left
    failure_domainwarningMembers that must be apart share a failure domain (Dedicated instances, HA and moves)
    files_share_backupswarningA region with stored files has no files target of its own
    capacity_proposalwarningA capacity proposal waits for approval
    capacity_failedcriticalA provisioning failed in the last 24 h (Billing, Free tier and capacity)

    Firing, deduplication and clearing#

    A condition's key is kind:target_type:target_id. Evaluate upserts each holding condition against a unique index on the key WHERE status = 'firing', so it opens a row or refreshes the firing one (xmax = 0 tells which), and resolves every firing row whose key did not come up. A condition that returns opens a new row. The grace periods are kept in each process's memory (poolerFailing).

    Risk
    • Nothing holds a resolved alert down. Thresholds have no hysteresis and one good evaluation resolves. A node's disk hovering at 85% as WAL is recycled, or a project at its disk warning, fires and resolves at each crossing, every 30 s at worst, each time a new row and two notifications. With several servers the grace clocks are per process, so one server resolves what another just fired. The alerts table is never pruned, so flapping also grows it. Resolving only after a few clear evaluations would cover all three.
    • A failed on-demand restore test of a deleted project never clears. FailedLatestOperations groups by project and keeps soft-deleted ones, and the restore_test case, unlike the backup one, does not check the project is live. Weekly tests run with no project and never replace that row. So "Restore test of failed" fires for good, and through States keeps the public page's Backups component degraded; for a live project, until someone tests it again. Alerts cannot be dismissed.
    • One failing source silences every alert. conditions returns nothing when any query fails, so Evaluate neither resolves nor fires. A query that keeps failing (a bug, a lock, a slow WALArchiveSamples over a large metric_points) leaves a log line every 30 s and no alert. Firing what was read while resolving nothing would keep decision M7 #1's protection.

    Delivery#

    Channels are one webhook and one SMTP account, kept in the alerts settings row with the webhook secret and SMTP password sealed under the master key (Save). The API shows secrets only as present. DeliverPending claims up to 50 notifications at a time:

    A failure sets the lock to 1 min × 2^attempts, capped at 30 min. With no channel configured, the notification is marked handled. Each event goes to every channel:

    The webhook is a JSON POST with X-Xenibase-Event (alert.firing, alert.resolved, alert.test), 10 s to answer 2xx, and, with a secret, X-Xenibase-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "t.body"> (alerts.Sign). The payload is the alert's id, kind, severity, summary, target, times and detail. It goes through a plain HTTP client, not the outbound one: the URL is the platform admin's. Email is plain text over STARTTLS (required when chosen), implicit TLS, or none for a local relay; a subject with anything outside printable ASCII is RFC 2047-encoded, so a name cannot add a header. Settings → Alerts → Test sends alert.test to each channel.

    Risk
    • One broken channel resends to the working one. deliver joins both channels' errors and the whole notification is retried on both. With email misconfigured, the webhook gets each firing again every 30 minutes for 7 days, about 340 times; with the webhook down, the inbox does. A scratch test (webhook answering 200, SMTP on a closed port) saw one firing three times in three claims. Recording delivery per channel would fix it.
    • An alert that resolves before its first successful delivery is never sent. The claim takes a resolved alert only if its firing was notified, so while delivery fails any alert shorter than the backoff vanishes unannounced.

    Metrics#

    Collect runs every XENIBASE_METRICS_INTERVAL (1 min) on every server. Per instance it opens one admin connection and reads each database's counters from pg_stat_database and client backends from pg_stat_activity, with pg_database_size every 5 min, and a dedicated instance's archiver (Backups, restores and imports). TPS and cache hit ratio are deltas, skipped when a counter went backwards. The poolers' SHOW POOLS gives clients and waiting clients, and their transaction counters mark projects active for the Free tier (Billing, Free tier and capacity). Node metrics come from the agents' last health checks, when fresh.

    ScopeMetrics
    projectsize_bytes, connections_active, connections_idle, pooler_clients, pooler_waiting, tps, cache_hit_ratio; dedicated only: wal_archive_failed, wal_archive_age_s, wal_archive_pending, wal_archive_pending_age_s
    nodecpu_percent, load1, mem_used_bytes, mem_total_bytes, disk_used_bytes, disk_total_bytes, disk_read_bps, disk_write_bps

    Points go into metric_points, keyed by scope, id, metric, resolution and minute, with an upsert, so several servers or a restart do not duplicate a point. Hourly (and at start, for the last 25 hours) the collector averages completed hours into 1h points and prunes: 1m points after 24 hours, 1h after 30 days (PruneMetrics), over an index on (resolution, ts). The API serves 1 h and 24 h from minute points and 7 d from hourly ones, adding live averages for the hours not yet downsampled (Query). A project's metrics are ProjectView and add the top 10 statements from pg_stat_statements when the project enabled it; a node's are the platform admin's.

    The Prometheus endpoint#

    GET /metrics serves the latest value of every series from the last max(3 × interval, 6 min) as gauges xenibase_project_* and xenibase_node_*, plus xenibase_up and the audit writer's own counters, which matter most when the database refuses writes. The route is public in the route table; the handler checks:

    XENIBASE_METRICS_TOKEN must be at least 24 characters. Project series are labelled project_id, org_id, org and tier, never by project or database name, since a project's name is its tenant's; node series by node_id and node. Label values are escaped. Cardinality is bounded by the platform's own size: at most 11 series per live project (deleted ones drop out) and 8 per node, with nothing per request, user or query. Renaming an organisation changes its org label and so starts new series.

    Logging#

    Every binary builds its logger with logging.New: log/slog to stderr, JSON unless the format is text. The server takes XENIBASE_LOG_FORMAT and XENIBASE_LOG_LEVEL; the agent, edge and status page take their own *_LOG_FORMAT and log at info. The API's requestLogger writes one line per request with method, path, status, bytes, duration and request id. The path has no query string, and no body or header is logged. Paths carry ids, and on two routes a billing contact's email or a support phone number, but no secret.

    What is never logged: secrets (the import and Supabase helpers strip passwords from connection errors), and SQL. The console's audit entry has the statement count, the read-only flag and the error code, never the text (The control plane). The one secret logged on purpose is the first-run setup code, which works only until the first operator exists. Postgres itself logs any statement over 5 s (log_min_duration_statement) with its text, in the container's log; log_statement stays none, and the isolation check fails a cluster where it is not.

    Risk
    • Container logs are never rotated. No service sets logging: and the install guide does not configure the daemon, whose default json-file driver keeps everything. A line per API request and every slow tenant statement's text pile up on the databases' disk until it fills. A max-size and max-file per service would bound it.
    • Secret files take the default umask. upgrade.sh creates its dump (password hashes, verifiers, every sealed secret) under the shell's umask, usually 0644, in a 0755 directory, and chmod 600s it only after pg_dump ends. An .env copied by hand from .env.example, as its first line suggests, keeps the copy's mode; install.sh never tightens it. It matters only with other local users, but umask 077 in both scripts costs nothing.

    The status page: xenibase-status#

    xenibase-status is a separate pure-Go binary with one SQLite file (V3 §2.6), meant for another provider so an outage cannot take down the page that reports it, and it never touches Xenibase's database. LoadConfig refuses unknown keys in status.toml, reads *_file secrets, and requires a push secret of at least 32 characters if one is set.

    Checks and automatic incidents#

    Every interval (1 min), Tick runs every component's probes at once from outside: http (a 2xx), postgres (a query through a DSN in a secret file) or tcp, 10 s each. Some failing is degraded, all failing is down. A heartbeat component takes xenibase-server's last report, or unknown after 5 min; with probes too, the worse wins.

    An automatic incident is auto-<component>-<unix>, major when down and minor when degraded, backdated to the first failing check, quoting the probe errors; xenibase-server's pushes cannot overwrite it (409). A component shows the worse of its measured state and any open manual incident naming it, and a measurement older than three intervals as no data.

    History#

    Each check records the worst state of the minute; each tick re-counts the last day into daily totals and drops minutes after 3 days and days after 90 (rollUp). The page draws 90 daily bars, with uptime counting degraded minutes as up and unknown ones as neither; /api/v1/status, /api/v1/incidents and /feed.rss serve the same. The HTML is html/template under a CSP of default-src 'none'.

    Signed pushes#

    Five endpoints take xenibase-server's requests: PUT /api/v1/incidents/{id}, POST /api/v1/heartbeat, PUT /api/v1/sla/targets, POST /api/v1/sla/results and PUT /api/v1/subscribers/managed. Each needs Xenibase-Signature, the same scheme as webhooks (Database webhooks and scheduled jobs), checked by one wrapper:

    Without a push secret every push is refused. A pushed incident must name its own id in the path and only known components; its updates are replaced as a set, and the ones with new ids are mailed. The heartbeat maps each state to the page's components of that heartbeat id, a region-specific state winning over a regionless one. The SLA endpoints are on Dedicated instances, HA and moves.

    Risk

    A push's signature is not bound to its endpoint. The HMAC covers the timestamp and body only, and unknown JSON fields are ignored. A signed heartbeat body sent to PUT /api/v1/subscribers/managed decodes as an empty list and deletes every managed subscriber; sent to /api/v1/sla/targets it removes every SLA target. A scratch test did both (204 twice, the list emptied). A heartbeat replayed within five minutes also overwrites a newer one. It needs someone who sees a signed request, one a minute, and XENIBASE_STATUS_URL may be http://. Signing the method and path too, and refusing an older heartbeat, would close it.

    Subscribers#

    With [smtp] set, anyone can subscribe (Subscribe): five requests an hour per client address, one confirmation mail per address per 10 minutes, the same answer whether or not the address is subscribed, a 48-hour link whose token is stored only as a SHA-256, and unconfirmed sign-ups dropped after 7 days. Links open a page whose button POSTs, so a mail scanner's prefetch changes nothing. Mail goes through an outbox, retried with backoff up to 10 times. Managed subscribers come from xenibase-server hourly (Subscribers): owners and billing contacts with status emails on, of active paying organisations, mailed without opt-in only for incidents on the components and regions their projects use. Unsubscribing removes the address from both lists and leaves a tombstone the syncs honour.

    Incidents from Xenibase#

    Platform admins write incidents in Admin → Incidents (incidents.Create, Post, Edit), on the components in XENIBASE_STATUS_COMPONENTS. A change clears pushed_at; every 10 s Push sends each unpushed incident whole and marks it pushed only if it did not change meanwhile, so a status page that was down catches up. The same loop sends the heartbeat every minute (backups, dedicated, webhooks and jobs, billing, backend services per region: what is wrong, never how much or for whom), syncs subscribers hourly, and closes announced maintenance whose window ended. Organisations see open incidents covering their projects in a banner.

    Risk

    Without a status page, maintenance never ends. main starts incidents.Run only when XENIBASE_STATUS_URL is set (here), yet Run has a branch for no status page whose only job is EndMaintenance. On an install without one, an announced window is never resolved and an unconfirmed draft never lapses, so every covered organisation's dashboard shows the finished maintenance as in progress until an admin resolves it by hand. Starting Run unconditionally would fix it.

    Note

    An automatic incident and a degraded component's line show the probes' error text on the public page, cut at 200 characters. A postgres probe's error names the probe's user, database and the address it reached.

    Support#

    internal/support keeps tickets in the metadata database (V3 §7.1), numbered T-n, each with a channel, status (open, pending, solved, closed), priority, the plan when it opened, an assignee and a response target. OpenTicket trims the subject to 200 characters, refuses a body over 20,000, inserts the ticket and its first message in one transaction, and acknowledges by the same channel.

    ChannelHow it is authenticatedWhich organisation
    Dashboard (POST /api/v1/orgs/{org}/support/tickets)The session; any member (OrgView)The path's
    Email (POST /api/v1/support/inbound/email)The email provider presents XENIBASE_SUPPORT_INBOUND_SECRET as basic auth or X-Xenibase-Inbound-Secret, compared in constant time. Bodies up to 4 MiB, in this API's fields or Postmark's.The sender's: an organisation it is a billing contact of, else its only membership, else none for staff to assign
    WhatsApp (POST /api/v1/support/whatsapp)X-Hub-Signature-256, HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the Meta app secret; the GET handshake checks the verify tokenThe organisation that registered the number, if on Pro or Team; other numbers get one reply pointing to email and the dashboard

    Threading. Outbound mail carries [T-n] in the subject and a recorded Message-ID. An inbound email joins a ticket by that reference, or by an In-Reply-To or References id Xenibase recorded, but only from the requester or a member of the ticket's organisation; anything else opens a new ticket. Quoted history is stripped, and a message id seen before changes nothing. A WhatsApp message joins the open ticket from its number; media become a placeholder line. Attachments are not stored at all (every message's attachments is []), so there is nothing to serve or sanitise yet.

    Response targets (TargetFor): Free is best effort with no target; Pro 8 business hours; Team 4; an urgent ticket on Pro or Team one hour of calendar time. Business hours are 09:00 to 17:00 WAT, Monday to Friday, without public holidays. A change of priority or organisation before the first response recomputes the target from the ticket's opening time.

    Who sees what. In the dashboard, owners and admins see all of their organisation's tickets; other members see the ones they opened, by user id or email (seesTicket). A ticket of another organisation answers 404. Internal notes (direction = 'note') never leave the support console, by email or the org API. The console is for platform admins and the support role (SupportConsole), and its context panel shows the organisation's metadata, never data (Identity, organisations and access).

    Risk

    Another organisation can claim a customer's tickets. Billing contacts and WhatsApp numbers are whatever an organisation's owners and admins type, unverified, and billing contacts rank first. If organisation A adds victim@b.example as a billing contact, every email the victim sends support opens a ticket in A: A's owners and admins read it and every staff reply in their dashboard, and A's members can reply into it by email, since the thread check accepts any member of the ticket's organisation. A scratch test reproduced both. A number registered by A does the same for WhatsApp (InboundWhatsApp), and B can no longer register it. Verifying an address or number by a code before it routes tickets would fix it.

    Risk

    An inbound email's sender is taken on trust. parseInboundEmail reads From and ignores the provider's SPF and DKIM verdicts; the inbound secret proves the provider called, not who wrote. Mail forged as an organisation's owner opens a ticket the console shows as the owner's, with the organisation's context, or, with the owner's sequential [T-n], joins the owner's thread. The forger reads no replies, but staff act on what tickets ask, and the acknowledgement from the genuine support address quotes the forged subject to the forged address. Flagging or refusing mail without a passing DMARC result would close it.

    Version and build information#

    internal/version holds Version, Commit and BuildDate, set with -ldflags -X; a plain go build reports 0.0.0-dev. The bundle takes VERSION from git describe --tags --always, exactly the tag on a tagged checkout, which upgrade.sh's gate relies on. Only the main Dockerfile sets the build date. Every binary answers -version, the server serves GET /api/v1/version without authentication, and agents report theirs in health checks; the server sends no work to an agent of another major or an older minor (Nodes and agents).

    Spec and code#

    Spec and code differ
    • V1 §11.1 has a curl … | sh installer and a bare-metal systemd path beside Compose. There is only the Compose bundle, and install.sh needs a git checkout.
    • V1 §11.3 says the server refuses to start if the agent version is incompatible. It starts, and refuses work to that agent.
    • V1 §8.7 exposes /metrics "for anyone who wants it". It needs the metrics token or a platform admin's session (decision M6 #9).
    • V3 §2.6 wants the 90-day history to use "the same measurements as the SLA". The page's history comes from its component probes; the SLA counts separate per-project probes from both vantage points (Dedicated instances, HA and moves).
    • V3 §7.1 gives the one-hour target to HA incidents. Any ticket the customer marks urgent on Pro or Team gets it.
    • docs/operations.md's alert table lists 12 of the 21 kinds, and calls the restore-test alert the weekly test's, though a test run on demand for one project raises its own.

    Failure handling#

    What failsWhat happens
    .env lacks a required variabledocker compose up refuses with the variable's message; nothing starts.
    upgrade.sh's checks failExit 1 with the reason; nothing changed.
    The metadata dump fails or looks wrongExit 1; nothing changed.
    install.sh fails, or the gates time outThe rollback stops the server and agent, restores the dump if the schema moved, checks out the previous release, reinstalls and runs the gates. Exit 2.
    The rollback failsExit 3 with the dump's path and the manual steps. The server may be stopped.
    An alert condition query failsNo alert fires or resolves that round; a warning is logged.
    A webhook or SMTP delivery failsThe notification retries on both channels with backoff to 30 min, for 7 days; the error is kept on the alert.
    An instance does not answer the collectorIts projects get no points that minute; the error is logged and other instances are sampled.
    xenibase-status is unreachableIncidents stay unpushed and are sent when it is back; the server logs the first failure and the recovery. The page shows heartbeat components as no data after 5 min.
    Xenibase is downProbes fail from outside; after three checks the page opens an incident by itself, and resolves it after two good ones.
    A push is unsigned, stale by over 5 min, or badly signed401, logged with the path and remote address.
    The inbound email secret is wrong or unset401; dashboard tickets and outbound replies still work.
    A WhatsApp webhook fails part-way500, so Meta retries; messages already threaded are skipped by their ids.
    Outbound support mail or WhatsApp failsLogged; the ticket and message are kept, and no Message-ID is recorded for mail not sent.
